item.title: Finding Your Balance on the Edge of the Andaman
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Banyan Tree Krabi has expanded its holistic wellness offering with the opening of the Mek Khram Wellbeing Centre, a dedicated facility for Pilates, Thai boxing and other guided fitness practices at its beachfront resort in southern Thailand. Equipped with reformer and Cadillac tables, the centre offers expert-led instruction for guests ranging from Pilates beginners to those seeking a more active introduction to Thailand’s traditional martial art. The new classes complement an established programme that includes Hatha yoga, tai chi, floating meditation, forest bathing and sailing, as well as the resort’s Rainforest hydrotherapy circuit at Banyan Tree Spa. Through its Wellbeing Sanctuary programme, guests can also develop personalized itineraries based on individual goals, combining movement, meditation, nutrition, spa treatments and restorative practices. With 72 pool suites and villas set between a tropical beachfront and mountainous landscape, the resort brings together active wellness and the slower rhythms of an Andaman Sea escape.

The Curated Take

Wellness travel has moved beyond the familiar promise of a spa treatment or a morning yoga class. At Banyan Tree Krabi, the emphasis is on creating a more integrated stay, where physical activity, cultural immersion and restorative practices can be shaped around the individual. The addition of Thai boxing is particularly fitting, introducing guests to a distinctly Thai discipline while offering a different kind of connection to the destination. For travelers seeking a luxury retreat that balances movement with genuine rest, the setting and breadth of the Wellbeing Sanctuary make wellness part of the journey rather than an amenity on the side.

item.title: The New Safari Luxury Is Having the Wilderness to Yourself
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
For discerning safari travelers, the definition of luxury is shifting from the most celebrated lodge to the freedom of experiencing the wilderness with fewer people and greater personal access. According to luxury tour operator Africa&You, requests for exclusive-use camps, private vehicles and private villas have increased 70% year over year, reflecting growing demand for privacy, flexibility and unhurried exploration. The company’s Where to Safari in 2027 selection highlights five destinations where that sense of space remains central: South Africa’s Eastern Cape, Zambia’s South Luangwa, Tanzania’s remote Katavi, Namibia’s Kunene and Skeleton Coast, and Botswana’s Makgadikgadi Pans. The report also points to a broader evolution in luxury safari travel, with guests favoring longer stays in fewer locations and experiences that extend beyond game drives to include walking safaris, conservation encounters, cultural connections and restorative time in nature. Together, these destinations offer a compelling view of safari’s next chapter, where exclusivity is measured not simply by the accommodation, but by the depth and individuality of the experience.

The Curated Take

There is a meaningful distinction between having a private vehicle and feeling that a landscape is truly yours. The appeal of these quieter safari regions lies in the opportunity to spend more time observing, listening and understanding a place, rather than moving quickly between celebrated wildlife sightings. From the immense salt flats of Botswana to Namibia’s desert coastline and Zambia’s walking-safari country, these journeys reward travelers willing to venture beyond the familiar circuits. The most valuable luxury may be the freedom to slow down, follow the guidance of someone who knows the land intimately, and experience Africa on a more personal scale.

item.title: Seoul Incheon’s oneworld Lounge Earns a Second Consecutive Year of Recognition
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The oneworld branded lounge at Seoul Incheon International Airport has been named “Asia’s Leading Airline Lounge - Business Class” at the 2026 World Travel Awards for the second consecutive year, reinforcing its reputation for premium airport hospitality. Opened in January 2024 as the alliance’s first branded lounge, the 555-square-metre space welcomes approximately 150,000 guests annually and serves eligible oneworld Emerald and Sapphire members, along with First and Business Class passengers. Its design draws inspiration from South Korean culture, with a bar influenced by the traditional gat hat and glass art recalling the Lantern Festival. Seasonally changing menus and distinct areas for dining, working and relaxing give travelers room to shape their time before departure. Seven oneworld member airlines serve the lounge at Incheon, including Cathay Pacific, Finnair, Qatar Airways and American Airlines.

The Curated Take

For travelers connecting through Seoul, the lounge offers more than a comfortable place to wait between flights. Its Korean design references and rotating menus bring a sense of destination into the airport experience, while its separate spaces recognize that pre-flight time can serve different purposes, from quiet restoration to a proper meal. As premium airport lounges become an increasingly important part of the luxury travel experience, oneworld’s continued recognition at Incheon highlights the value of thoughtful hospitality before the journey even begins.

item.title: Bangkok Takes the Festive Season to New Heights at INNSiDE by Meliá
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
INNSiDE by Meliá Bangkok Sukhumvit is bringing a distinctly international flavor to the 2026 festive season, pairing Spanish cuisine, celebratory buffets and rooftop festivities with sweeping views of the Thai capital. The 208-room hotel will mark Christmas and New Year across three elevated venues: LUZ Bangkok Tapas Bar, where Madrid-born chef Juan Ignacio García Racionero will prepare Spanish-inspired holiday menus; The Kites Eatery, which will host Christmas and New Year’s Eve buffets overlooking the city; and the 34th-floor Giant Swing Pool Bar, the setting for a countdown celebration welcoming 2027. The hotel’s design also draws on local references, from the pool bar’s interpretation of Bangkok’s historic Giant Swing to artwork at The Kites Eatery inspired by traditional kite-flying at Sanam Luang Park. Together, the dining and entertainment program offers travelers a festive city stay that brings together Spanish culinary influences, Bangkok character and the energy of a rooftop celebration.

The Curated Take

Bangkok offers a different kind of festive escape, one shaped by warm evenings, a dynamic dining scene and a skyline that becomes part of the celebration. INNSiDE by Meliá Bangkok Sukhumvit gives the season a sense of occasion without relying on traditional winter imagery, while its Spanish restaurant and Thai design references create an interesting meeting of cultures. For travelers spending Christmas or New Year in Thailand, the hotel provides a lively urban alternative to a resort-based holiday.

item.title: The Art of Spending an Afternoon in Yountville
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Hotel Yountville is welcoming day visitors and local residents to experience more of its vineyard estate-inspired retreat in the heart of California’s Napa Valley, expanding access beyond registered overnight guests. The newly opened public offerings include seasonal, farm-to-table dining at Heritage Oak, specialty cocktails and light bites at The Y Bar Lounge & Terrace, and restorative treatments at The Spa at Hotel Yountville. Spa experiences range from massage therapies and bathing rituals to facials and body treatments, with pool access included for guests receiving services. Set within the walkable town of Yountville, the property brings together Tuscan villa-inspired accommodations, a cypress-lined pool courtyard, and an intimate collection of dining and wellness experiences, offering another way to enjoy the region beyond its celebrated wineries and tasting rooms. Napa County residents are also being welcomed with special introductory benefits through April 30, 2027.

The Curated Take

Napa Valley is often explored through its vineyards, tasting rooms, and destination restaurants, but the appeal of wine country also lies in knowing when to slow down. Hotel Yountville’s expanded public access makes it possible to enjoy a leisurely lunch, an afternoon at the spa, or cocktails on the terrace without planning an overnight stay. For travelers already exploring Yountville, it adds another dimension to a day in one of Napa Valley’s most celebrated towns.

item.title: Universal Epic Universe Expands Its Dark Universe with a New Indoor Thrill Coaster
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Universal Orlando Resort is preparing to add another high-energy attraction to Universal Epic Universe, announcing an all-new indoor thrill coaster for the park’s Dark Universe land. Additional details about the ride have yet to be revealed, but the announcement signals another step in the resort’s ongoing expansion of its theme park and entertainment offerings. The new coaster joins a broader development slate across the destination, including a reimagined Universal Horror Make-Up Show featuring Blumhouse at Universal Studios Florida, the high-speed Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift coaster planned for 2027, a new signature restaurant in the Jurassic Park area of Universal Islands of Adventure, and Luke Combs’ Category 10 music and entertainment venue at Universal CityWalk. Together, these projects point to a growing mix of attractions, dining and live entertainment designed to give visitors new reasons to build a longer Orlando stay.

The Curated Take

For travelers considering Orlando, the destination’s appeal increasingly extends beyond a single park or headline attraction. Continued investment across Epic Universe, Universal Studios Florida, Islands of Adventure and CityWalk creates more possibilities for repeat visitors and longer stays, particularly for those who want to combine immersive attractions with dining and evening entertainment. The new Dark Universe coaster remains under wraps, but its announcement adds another reason to keep an eye on what is taking shape at Universal Orlando.

item.title: At Vyn, the Flavors of Southern Sweden Earn a Place Among the World’s Best
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Restaurant Vyn, the two-Michelin-starred destination led by chef Daniel Berlin, has climbed to No. 23 on the 2026 list of The 50 Best Restaurants, rising 24 places from its position last year and bringing international attention to Österlen, a coastal region in southeastern Skåne. Set near the fishing village of Brantevik with views across the Baltic Sea, Vyn draws its identity from the surrounding landscape, with a seasonal approach shaped by local farmers, regional producers, foraging and the traditions of southern Sweden. The restaurant is part of a larger hospitality experience that includes a 15-room boutique hotel, a food and wine bar, and private dining, making it possible to extend a culinary visit into a longer stay. Beyond the table, Österlen offers a rich setting for exploration, with fertile farmland, apple orchards, vineyards, fishing villages, sandy beaches and a growing community of artisan food producers.

The Curated Take

Vyn’s recognition offers a compelling reason to look beyond Sweden’s better-known urban destinations and discover the quieter culinary character of Österlen. Here, fine dining is not separated from its surroundings; the ingredients, producers and changing seasons are integral to the experience. For travelers who plan journeys around food, Vyn provides an anchor for exploring a region where farm shops, local vineyards, coastal landscapes and small villages contribute to a broader sense of place. The appeal is not simply a celebrated restaurant, but the opportunity to understand southern Sweden through the people and flavors that define it.

item.title: Give the Gift of Country: Discover Australia Through Its First Nations Cultures
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
As travelers and gift-givers reconsider the environmental cost of seasonal consumption, Discover Aboriginal Experiences is offering a more meaningful way to celebrate: sharing a connection to Country through Aboriginal-led tourism and Indigenous-created art. The collective brings together more than 50 Aboriginal tourism operators across Australia, with more than 200 experiences spanning urban and regional destinations. Visitors can explore ancient rock art galleries in Cape York with Jarramali Rock Art Tours, learn about Tjukurpa on Anangu Country with SEIT Australia, discover Sydney’s Indigenous heritage while climbing the Harbour Bridge with Burrawa Aboriginal Climb Experience, or follow the cultural and ecological stories of Tasmania’s northeast coast on the four-day wukalina Walk. Other experiences include guided walks, native food encounters, cultural storytelling and opportunities to purchase art and handcrafted works directly from Indigenous creatives. Beyond offering an alternative to conventional holiday gifts, these experiences support Aboriginal-owned businesses, cultural preservation and a deeper understanding of the world’s oldest living cultures.

The Curated Take

Some of the most meaningful souvenirs are not objects at all, but the knowledge and perspective carried home from a place. First Nations tourism offers travelers an opportunity to understand Australia through the voices of its Traditional Owners, connecting landscape, history, culture and contemporary community life. Whether through a guided journey on Country or artwork acquired directly from its creator, these gifts carry a significance beyond the festive season. They also invite a more thoughtful approach to travel, one in which cultural exchange and care for the land are central to the experience.

item.title: Maui Invites Visitors to Discover the Cultural and Ecological Importance of Limu
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
An often-overlooked part of Hawaiʻi’s coastal environment takes center stage at Maui Ocean Center, where a new exhibit introduces visitors to limu, the diverse marine algae traditionally gathered and used throughout the islands. Opening November 12, the exhibit currently features four varieties of limu, with plans to expand the collection and eventually develop seed stock to support restoration projects around Maui. The opening celebration will bring together cultural and community organizations, including Ke Kīpuka Limu and Waimānalo Limu Hui, for hands-on educational activities exploring the ecological and cultural significance of these marine plants. Visitors can also experience limu-inspired food offerings and attend an evening educational program featuring specialists and aquaculturists. The initiative extends beyond the aquarium, with a community restoration project planned for Lāhainā the following day. Through the exhibit, Maui Ocean Center offers another perspective on Hawaiʻi’s marine environment, connecting coastal ecology, traditional knowledge and ongoing conservation efforts.

The Curated Take

Understanding a destination often begins with looking more closely at what lies beneath the familiar attractions. Limu is woven into Hawaiian foodways, cultural practices and the health of nearshore ecosystems, making this exhibit an opportunity to explore a meaningful part of the islands’ natural and cultural heritage. For visitors to Maui, it adds depth to an ocean-focused itinerary, moving beyond the beauty of the coastline to consider the knowledge, relationships and restoration work that help sustain it.

item.title: The 72: Manhattan, Dressed for Christmas
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Luxury travel doesn’t always require a week away, let alone two. For travelers whose calendars are already spoken for, the prospect of a longer escape can make even the most enticing destination feel out of reach. Yet a long weekend can open a very different kind of door. A city experienced in concentrated, carefully chosen moments can be every bit as memorable as a longer stay. The secret is knowing what deserves your time.

Welcome to The 72, Curated’s approach to making extraordinary travel fit real life. Each edition takes a destination and distills it into 72 hours, balancing its defining experiences with the discoveries that make it worth the journey. Consider it permission to stop waiting for the perfect two-week window. Sometimes, three days are enough to begin a love affair with a place.

Where to Stay: A Christmas Classic

Some hotels are so entwined with a city’s identity that staying there becomes part of the destination itself. At Christmas, few places capture Manhattan’s grand holiday fantasy quite like The Plaza. Set at the southeast corner of Central Park, the storied hotel puts Fifth Avenue’s festive displays, the park and Midtown’s seasonal landmarks within easy reach. Inside, the Palm Court’s soaring stained-glass dome and elegant afternoon tea offer a welcome pause from the bustle outside. For guests who want to take the celebration back to their room, The Plaza’s seasonal Suitest Season of All package features a decorated seven-foot Christmas tree and holiday welcome amenities. It is an invitation to make the hotel part of the Christmas experience, rather than simply a place to return at night.

For a different expression of Manhattan glamour, The Carlyle brings Upper East Side elegance, intimate dining and live music into the holiday season. Meanwhile, Mandarin Oriental, New York, overlooking Central Park from Columbus Circle, offers contemporary luxury and a dramatic panorama of the city. Choose The Plaza for the classic Christmas story, The Carlyle for discreet old-New York sophistication, or Mandarin Oriental for a modern retreat above the park.

Culture Beyond the Christmas Crowds

Even in December, Manhattan offers more than festive façades and seasonal spectacles. The Morgan Library & Museum is a compelling place to begin, with its richly decorated historic library, rare books and manuscripts, and the intimate atmosphere of a collection once assembled by financier J. Pierpont Morgan. It feels like entering a private world of scholarship and collecting, a quieter counterpoint to the crowds outside.

At the Museum of Modern Art, spend time with Vincent van Gogh’s The Starry Night, then follow your curiosity through a collection that changed how the world sees modern art. For travelers who prefer a more personal encounter, a private art-historian tour is worth investigating. The Metropolitan Museum of Art offers another direction entirely, with galleries that span centuries and cultures. With only 72 hours, choose one major museum and give it enough time to be rewarding rather than racing through all three.

The Morgan has a particularly fitting seasonal event on December 15, 2026: A Christmas Carol, a musical interpretation of Dickens’s classic narrated by Christine Baranski, with choral music woven into the story. The performance is currently sold out, with a waitlist available, making it a date-specific possibility for travelers lucky enough to secure tickets.

Christmas Shopping, New York Style

Christmas shopping in Manhattan is as much about looking as buying. The Fifth Avenue windows turn retail into theatre, with each store interpreting the season through its own visual language. Start at Tiffany & Co., where the flagship’s celebrated blue-box identity extends into the holiday windows. Inside, the Blue Box Café offers Breakfast at Tiffany’s, a stylish way to begin the day before browsing the jewellery and collections. Reservations are essential, and the café is an experience in its own right.

Continue to Cartier at 653 Fifth Avenue, where the mansion-like flagship has traditionally been transformed into an enormous red Christmas present. At Bergdorf Goodman, pause to study the elaborate windows, renowned for their intricate craftsmanship and imaginative storytelling. Then make your way to Saks Fifth Avenue, opposite Rockefeller Center, where the windows and façade have long been part of the city’s holiday spectacle. The exact displays change every year, which is part of the pleasure: the experience belongs to this particular Christmas.

Leave room for the smaller discoveries between the famous addresses. Browse the luxury boutiques along Fifth and Madison Avenues, stop for a warming drink, and resist the temptation to rush. In Manhattan at Christmas, window-shopping is not a substitute for shopping. It is one of the reasons to come.

Manhattan, Dressed for Christmas

There is a reason the Rockefeller Center Christmas tree remains one of the city’s defining seasonal sights. Standing beneath its lights, with the skating rink below and the surrounding buildings glowing after dark, is a familiar scene that somehow retains its power in person. Arrive with time to enjoy the setting rather than simply take a photograph and move on. For a more elevated perspective, investigate Rockefeller Center’s VIP holiday experiences, including private rooftop and skating options, and confirm which packages and tree-related experiences are available for your dates.

The Fifth Avenue windows are best enjoyed after dusk, when the displays glow against the winter evening. From there, continue to Bryant Park Winter Village, where market stalls, seasonal food and the skating rink create a different kind of Christmas atmosphere. Wander through the stalls, browse for gifts and warm up with hot chocolate. It is an easy place to linger without an agenda, and a lovely way to spend an evening after a day of museums and shopping.

For travelers who want a more cinematic view of the city, a private carriage ride through Central Park can offer a quieter perspective on the season. Wrapped in a blanket, with the park’s winter landscape around you and the city just beyond its edges, the experience feels less like sightseeing and more like stepping into a New York Christmas scene.

The Art of Holiday Tea

Afternoon tea is one of Manhattan’s most enduring winter rituals, and the setting matters as much as the menu. At The Plaza’s Palm Court, tea becomes an occasion beneath the room’s magnificent stained-glass dome. Seasonal pastries and savouries, a traditional tea service and the hotel’s grand interiors make this the quintessential choice for a Christmas visit. Book ahead, particularly for holiday dates.

For a more fashion-forward experience, return to the Blue Box Café at Tiffany’s for Tea at Tiffany’s. It pairs the pleasure of a carefully presented tea service with the glamour of the Fifth Avenue flagship, making it an especially natural addition to a day spent exploring the holiday windows.

At MO Lounge in Mandarin Oriental, afternoon tea comes with sweeping views over Central Park. The atmosphere is contemporary and polished, with the winter landscape providing a beautiful backdrop. Each offers a different mood: The Plaza for old-world tradition, Tiffany’s for a distinctly New York fashion fantasy, and Mandarin Oriental for the view. Choose one and savour it rather than trying to fit all three into a single weekend.

Where to Eat: From Michelin Stars to Manhattan’s New Scene

In a city where a memorable meal can be the centrepiece of an evening, it is worth reserving one dinner for an experience that demands attention. Sushi Sho, near the New York Public Library, holds three Michelin stars in the 2025 guide. Chef Keiji Nakazawa’s Japanese omakase unfolds at an intimate hinoki counter, with a progression of seafood, vegetables and carefully developed flavours that rewards diners who enjoy watching a master at work. It is a serious splurge and a reservation to plan well in advance.

For a different expression of fine dining, Daniel brings French cuisine and polished service to the Upper East Side. Its seasonal menus make it a natural choice for a celebratory dinner, particularly for travelers whose dates coincide with its special holiday offerings. Those who prefer the energy of a fashionable New York night can look toward the city’s contemporary restaurant scene, where inventive menus and lively dining rooms offer a different kind of occasion. The right choice depends on the evening you want: a quiet, meticulously paced tasting menu, a classic fine-dining celebration or a restaurant that feels part of the city’s current conversation.

Whichever direction you choose, reserve the important dinner before building the rest of the evening around it. During the festive season, the most sought-after tables are part of the planning, not a last-minute decision.

The Main Event: Christmas on Stage

For many visitors, the evening performance is the moment that turns a holiday trip into a memory. Manhattan offers no shortage of choices, from the grand traditions of ballet to Broadway’s latest productions and the warmth of a concert hall.

Our first recommendation is New York City Ballet’s George Balanchine’s The Nutcracker at Lincoln Center. Tchaikovsky’s score, the scale of the production and the ballet’s intricate visual world make it a natural Christmas-night choice. It is festive without being frantic, and a particularly lovely way to close a short escape. Check the performance calendar for your dates and book early.

For travelers who want a full-scale holiday spectacle, the Radio City Christmas Spectacular starring the Rockettes is the alternative. Precision choreography, elaborate stage effects and familiar seasonal scenes make it an exuberant New York tradition. It is a different mood from the ballet, and both have their place. The choice comes down to whether you prefer the elegance of The Nutcracker or the high-energy spectacle of the Rockettes.

Music lovers can make an evening of Carnegie Hall, where the 2026 holiday calendar includes the New York Pops’ Sleigh Bells Ring on December 19 and the Vienna Boys Choir on December 20. The historic hall adds its own sense of occasion, whether the music leans toward familiar seasonal favourites or the purity of choral singing.

For theatre-goers who want something beyond the traditional Christmas production, Broadway’s late-2026 season brings several notable options. Aaron Sorkin’s A Few Good Men offers a gripping courtroom drama, while Much Ado About Nothing brings Shakespeare to the stage with Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell. The Fantasticks, making its Broadway debut, offers another direction for those interested in a fresh interpretation of a classic. These productions have limited scheduled runs, so check performance dates and ticket availability before committing to a particular evening.

And for a more literary Christmas, the Morgan’s A Christmas Carol, narrated by Christine Baranski and accompanied by choral music, offers a distinctive alternative for travelers visiting on December 15. It is a limited-date event, and tickets are currently sold out with a waitlist available, but it captures the kind of seasonal experience that makes planning ahead worthwhile.

Your 72 Hours, Your Way

The beauty of Manhattan at Christmas is that no single itinerary can contain it. One traveler might begin with Breakfast at Tiffany’s, spend the afternoon among the Fifth Avenue windows and end with a Michelin-starred dinner. Another might choose the Morgan, a concert at Carnegie Hall and an evening wandering Bryant Park. A third might make the ballet the centrepiece of the trip, with tea at The Plaza and time to take in the tree and the city lights.

Choose the experiences that speak to you, book the moments that matter most, and leave enough space for the unplanned discoveries in between. Three days may not be enough to see everything Manhattan offers at Christmas. They are enough to experience a version of it that feels entirely your own.
